details:
Universe Eye (عين الكون) is an AI-powered space exploration platform developed by The Supernova Team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, targeting the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. Its core goal is to clarify space imagery, analyze data from NASA's SPHEREx telescope, and detect Planet X alongside other cosmic anomalies.

The Problem It Solves

  • Massive, Noisy Data: NASA's SPHEREx telescope surveys the entire sky across 102 infrared spectral bands, producing vast amounts of noisy raw data.
  • Detecting Faint Objects: Cold and extremely faint celestial bodies like Planet X are difficult to identify amid visual noise and millions of known stars.
  • Data Security & Hallucination Risks: Using public cloud AI on sensitive or unpublished astronomical observations creates risks of data leakage and scientific hallucination.

Four-Stage System Pipeline

  1. Data Ingestion: Retrieves raw astronomical images and celestial coordinates (RA, Dec) directly from NASA telescope archives.
  2. Pre-Analysis Visual Enhancement: Cleans imagery before AI inspection using denoising, local contrast enhancement (CLAHE), and Unsharp Masking to highlight edges and craters. Users can choose Auto-Optimize or Manual Controls—including lighting balance and a Thermal Map—to view live Before vs. After comparisons of the Moon, planets, and deep-sky objects.
  3. Astronomical Cross-Matching & Filtering: Checks object coordinates against global catalogs (SIMBAD, NASA Exoplanets, and SkyBoT) to filter out previously known stars, planets, and asteroids, while also rejecting non-astronomical images to maintain scientific accuracy.
  4. AI Anomaly Classification & Thermal Analysis: Analyzes unregistered objects, classifies them (Planet X Candidate, Supernova, Star Collision, or Space Anomaly), and estimates their temperatures in Kelvin and Celsius.

Key Features & Capabilities

  • Thermal & Planetary Observatory: Computes daily planetary temperatures from their instantaneous distance from the Sun using Kepler's equations and NASA JPL Horizons data, while using infrared temperature estimates to distinguish cold candidates like Planet X (-50°C) from hotter stars and supernovae.
  • Bilingual Multi-Image Workspace: Provides a Dark Space HUD Theme (space navy, glowing cyan, and purple/gold accents) with one-click switching between Arabic and English, supporting direct imports from NASA's library, user uploads, and live camera capture.

Prototype vs. Production Architecture

  • Hackathon Prototype: Uses an interactive web interface connected to the Gemini 2.5 Flash Vision API for rapid processing and live demonstrations.
  • Full-Scale Production System: Designed to operate 100% locally / on-premise within air-gapped GPU clusters at observatories and space agencies using locally trained open-weight vision-language models (such as Qwen-VL, LLaVA, or PyTorch Custom CNNs). This keeps raw astronomical data completely confidential without relying on external servers or internet connectivity.

Tech Stack & Data Sources

  • Telescope Data & Archives: NASA SPHEREx, NASA/IPAC IRSA, WISE, and 2MASS.
  • Python Astronomical Libraries: Astropy (WCS coordinate conversion and FITS processing), Astroquery, and Photutils.
  • Live NASA & Global Catalog APIs: NASA Image and Video Library API, NASA Exoplanet Archive API, NASA JPL Horizons, SIMBAD TAP API, CDS Aladin HiPS2FITS, and IMCCE SkyBoT.
  • Processing & Frontend: OpenCV, HTML5 Canvas, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, and Gemini Vision API (in the prototype).

Impact & Roadmap

The project aims to accelerate SPHEREx discoveries, substantially reduce the time humans spend manually inspecting telescope imagery, and expand toward full local edge/server AI deployment in observatories and universities.
